title: Thiakry ou Dégué
author: Amina Savoura (Afrik)
desc: Steamed millet granules tossed with raisins, folded into a chilled mixture of soured milk (or plain yoghurt), evaporated milk and sugar — printed with several missing and unused ingredients, all recorded.
longDesc: Afrik’s thiakry or dégué: millet granules are steamed in a couscoussier until fully cooked, spread on a plate and loosened, with washed raisins added. The cream is the soured milk or yoghurt beaten in a bowl with fresh cream and unsweetened milk until homogeneous, with sugar and vanilla sugar and diced pineapple. The couscous goes in a salad bowl, the cream is added, mixed, and served very cold. The page’s ingredient list and method do not match: crème fraîche and pineapple are used but not listed; fromage blanc is listed but not used; and ‘500 g de farine de mil’ cannot be steamed in a couscoussier — the method says ‘granules’.
ingredients: 500 g millet flour (the method steams ‘granules’ — see the note)
1 litre soured milk (lait caillé), or 5 plain stirred yoghurts for those who don’t like soured milk
500 g fromage blanc — listed, not used in the method
1 tin unsweetened evaporated milk (Gloria brand named; volume not printed)
Fresh cream (crème fraîche) — used in the method, not in the list; quantity not printed
Diced pineapple — used in the method, not in the list; quantity not printed
steps: Put water in a pot that can hold a couscoussier. Pour the millet granules into the couscoussier and steam.
After complete cooking, remove the contents, place on a plate and loosen the grains. Wash and clean the raisins and add them to the thiakry.
Pour the soured milk or yoghurt into a large bowl with the fresh cream and the unsweetened milk. Beat until you get a homogeneous liquid.
Add the vanilla sugar and sugar. Add the diced pineapple.
Put the thiakry in a salad bowl, add the mixture, stir and serve very cold.
chefTips: The only usable cue printed is for the cream: ‘beat until you get a homogeneous liquid’; the steaming has no time (‘après cuisson complète’).
Use granulated millet couscous (araw/thiakry grain), not flour — the method steams granules.
Serve very cold, as the page says.
commonMistakes: Steaming millet flour as printed in the ingredient list.
Adding all the sugar at once — the page invites adjusting.
Serving the thiakry and cream mixed too long ahead — it thickens.
healthBenefits: Millet is gluten-free; soured milk is a source of calcium and probiotics.
culturalNote: Lait caillé appears as a bought ingredient with no souring step; the only sensory cue for it in the research (Gret/Enda Graf, 2005) is ‘acidulé, légèrement pétillant sur la langue’ — tart, slightly fizzing on the tongue — and describes the milk, not a step. Compare the Webb/RPCV printing, a wheat-couscous, yoghurt, half-and-half adaptation that is not recorded here as a Senegalese printing.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Thiakry ou dégué’. Byline: Amina Savoura. Publication: Afrik (afrik.com), category Culture. Date: ‘Publié le 16 avril 2012 à 16h28’. Yield: ‘Pour 10 Personne(s)’. TWO-PASS, identical.

DISCREPANCIES unreconciled, confirmed on both passes: crème fraîche and pineapple used but not listed; fromage blanc listed but not used; ‘farine de mil’ listed but ‘granulés’ steamed; the steaming has no time or temperature (‘après cuisson complète’ is circular).
FERMENTATION RULE — NO CUE, NO TIME: lait caillé is an ingredient only; the page describes no souring step.
ABSENT, not estimated: raisin quantity; evaporated-milk volume (‘1 boite de lait non sucré gloria’).
